To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tRNA binding to ribosomes can be measured by energy transfer and that tRNAs with labeled 3' ends bind to ribosomes in vitro.
the 3'-termini of tRNAs are in close proximity to the peptidyl transferase center and to each other when bound to ribosomes.
The distance between the 3’ termini of two tRNA molecules bound simultaneously on the ribosome can be measured by energy transfer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of tRNA and the ribosome.
the interaction of tRNAs with ribosomes and the mechanism of action of erythromycins.
the binding of tRNAs to ribosomes and the structure of ribosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3' terminus of the tRNAs is not in direct contact with the ribosomal subunits, but is rather in the close proximity of the ribosomal subunit.
the distance between two 3'-end labels on a tRNA bound to the ribosome is 34 A.
the fluorescently labeled tRNA can bind to ribosomes in a site specific manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ribosomal P and A sites can bind tRNA with a 3'-end label and that this label can be used to study the structure of the ribosomal P site.
the 3' terminus of a tRNA can be used to measure distances on the ribosome.
we have shown that tRNAs can be modified at their 3' terminus without affecting their ability to bind to ribosomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fluorescent tRNA probes can be used to determine the location of tRNAs on the ribosome.
the fluorescent 3' end is a useful probe for the ribosome and tRNA.
the ribosome can bind two tRNAs simultaneously in an extended configuration.
